title: TLS handshake failed (generic)
plain_english: The TLS handshake between the client and the server broke off before completing. If a more specific signature (unknown CA, expired certificate) was also detected, trust that one — this generic failure is what's left when the client aborts without saying why, or when protocol versions/ciphers simply don't overlap.

causes.cause: TLS version mismatch — old supplicants (printers, scanners, embedded devices) may only speak TLS 1.0/1.1 while the server enforces a higher minimum.
causes.next_check: Check tls_min_version in mods-available/eap and what the failing device supports; test by temporarily lowering the minimum for that device class.

causes.cause: The user cancelled a certificate-trust prompt on the device, so the supplicant tore the handshake down.
causes.next_check: Reproduce on a device you can watch: does a 'trust this certificate?' dialog appear at connect time?

causes.cause: No common cipher suite between the client and the server's OpenSSL policy.
causes.next_check: Look a few lines above the failure in radiusd -X for the ClientHello details, and review cipher_list in the eap TLS configuration.
